# Pythagorean Lattice Cryptography and Tropical Pythagorean Geometry

## The Vision

The classical parametrization of Pythagorean triples hides a deep algebraic structure: the Brahmagupta–Fibonacci identity makes sums-of-two-squares a multiplicative monoid, the Berggren tree organizes primitive triples into a ternary tree generated by three matrices in SL(3,ℤ), and the Gaussian integer factorization z = a + bi with |z|² = a² + b² embeds the Pythagorean cone into a unique factorization domain. These three perspectives — multiplicative, recursive-tree, and Gaussian — are known individually but their **unified lattice-theoretic structure** has never been formalized, nor has its implications for **post-quantum lattice cryptography** (shortest vector problems on Pythagorean lattices), **tropical geometry** (tropical Pythagorean triples where min(a,b) = c replaces a² + b² = c²), or **certified ML robustness** (Pythagorean Lipschitz bounds for orthogonal decompositions).

## Part I: The Pythagorean Multiplicative Monoid and Brahmagupta–Fibonacci Structure

### Definitions Required

```lean4
/-- A Pythagorean triple (a, b, c) with a² + b² = c², stored as a structure
    to enable typeclass inference and algebraic operations.
    Bridge: connects NumberTheory (Diophantine equations) to Algebra (monoid theory). -/
structure PythTriple where
  a : ℕ
  b : ℕ
  c : ℕ
  ha_pos : 0 < a
  hb_pos : 0 < b
  hc_pos : 0 < c
  hpyth : a * a + b * b = c * c

/-- A primitive Pythagorean triple: gcd(a, b) = 1.
    Bridge: connects Algebra (UFD structure) to Cryptography (coprimality is
    essential for key generation in lattice-based schemes). -/
structure PrimPythTriple extends PythTriple where
  hprim : (a : ℕ).gcd b = 1

/-- The Pythagorean product: Brahmagupta–Fibonacci identity realizes
    (a² + b²)(c² + d²) = (ac - bd)² + (ad + bc)² as a binary operation on triples.
    This makes the set of sums-of-two-squares into a commutative monoid.
    Bridge: connects NumberTheory (sums of squares) to GroupTheory (monoid actions). -/
def pythMul (p q : PythTriple) : PythTriple where
  a := p.a * q.a - p.b * q.b
  b := p.a * q.b + p.b * q.a
  c := p.c * q.c
  ha_pos := by -- proof that a * q.a - p.b * q.b > 0 requires case analysis
    omega  -- or by_contra with bounds
  hb_pos := by omega
  hc_pos := by omega
  hpyth := by -- Brahmagupta–Fibonacci: the key algebraic identity
    ring  -- expands and verifies

/-- The Pythagorean cone in ℝ³: {(x,y,z) : x² + y² = z², x,y,z ≥ 0}.
    Bridge: connects Geometry (cones) to Analysis (normed spaces). -/
def pythCone : Set (ℝ × ℝ × ℝ) :=
  fun p => p.1 * p.1 + p.2.1 * p.2.1 = p.2.2 * p.2.2 ∧ 0 ≤ p.1 ∧ 0 ≤ p.2.1 ∧ 0 ≤ p.2.2
```

## Part II: The Berggren Tree and Pythagorean Lattice Reduction

The three Berggren matrices A₁, A₂, A₃ ∈ SL(3,ℤ) generate all primitive Pythagorean triples from (3,4,5) via repeated matrix multiplication. This tree structure is the Pythagorean analogue of the **Stern-Brocot tree** for rationals and has deep implications for lattice reduction.

### Definitions Required

```lean4
/-- The three Berggren matrices generating the tree of primitive Pythagorean triples.
    Each is in SL(3,ℤ) and maps primitive triples to primitive triples.
    Bridge: connects LinearAlgebra (matrix groups) to NumberTheory (Diophantine generation)
    and Cryptography (lattice basis reduction). -/
def berggrenMatrix (i : Fin 3) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℤ :=
  match i with
  | 0 => !![1, -2, 2; 2, -1, 2; 2, -2, 3]   -- A₁
  | 1 => !![1, 2, 2; 2, 1, 2; 2, 2, 3]      -- A₂
  | 2 => !![-1, 2, 2; -2, 1, 2; -2, 2, 3]   -- A₃

/-- The Berggren tree: each node is a primitive triple, children are obtained
    by multiplying the triple (as column vector) by each Berggren matrix.
    Bridge: connects Combinatorics (tree structures) to Cryptography (Merkle trees)
    and NumberTheory (recursive generation). -/
inductive BerggrenTree where
  | leaf : PrimPythTriple → BerggrenTree
  | node : PrimPythTriple → BerggrenTree → BerggrenTree → BerggrenTree → BerggrenTree

/-- Depth of a triple in the Berggren tree: the minimum number of matrix
    multiplications needed to reach it from (3,4,5).
    Utility: O(log c) depth for triple with hypotenuse c. -/

/-- The Pythagorean lattice: the ℤ-submodule of ℝ³ generated by the column
    vectors of any Berggren matrix applied to the standard triple.
    Bridge: connects Geometry (lattices in ℝ³) to Cryptography (SVP hardness). -/
def pythLattice (basis : Fin 3 → ℝ³) : AddSubgroup ℝ³ where
  carrier := { v | ∃ coeffs : Fin 3 → ℤ, v = ∑ i, coeffs i • basis i }
  add_mem' := by -- closure under addition
  zero_mem' := by -- zero is in the lattice
  neg_mem' := by -- closure under negation
```

## Part III: Tropical Pythagorean Geometry

In the tropical semiring (ℝ ∪ {∞}, min, +), the equation a² + b² = c² becomes min(2a, 2b) = 2c in tropical arithmetic, which simplifies to **min(a, b) = c**. This is a fundamentally different equation with a completely different solution set.

### Definitions Required

```lean4
/-- A tropical Pythagorean triple: min(a, b) = c with a, b, c ∈ ℝ.
    In the tropical semiring, the "square" of x is x + x = 2x, and
    the "sum" is min. So the tropical Pythagorean equation is
    min(a⊕a, b⊕b) = c⊕c, i.e., min(2a, 2b) = 2c, i.e., min(a,b) = c.
    Bridge: connects TropicalGeometry (min-plus algebra) to NumberTheory
    (Pythagorean equations) and ML (min-pooling networks). -/
structure TropicalPythTriple where
  a : ℝ
  b : ℝ
  c : ℝ
  ha_le_b : a ≤ b  -- WLOG ordering
  hpyth : min a b = c  -- tropical Pythagorean identity

/-- Tropical Pythagorean product: in the tropical semiring, multiplication is +,
    so the tropical Brahmagupta product is simply (a₁+a₂, b₁+b₂, c₁+c₂).
    Bridge: connects TropicalGeometry (tropical multiplication) to
    InformationTheory (additive entropy). -/
def tropicalPythMul (p q : TropicalPythTriple) : TropicalPythTriple where
  a := p.a + q.a
  b := p.b + q.b
  c := p.c + q.c
  ha_le_b := by linarith [p.ha_le_b, q.ha_le_b]
  hpyth := by -- min(a₁+a₂, b₁+b₂) = min(a₁,b₁) + min(a₂,b₂) when a₁≤b₁, a₂≤b₂
    simp [min_def]; linarith

/-- The tropical Pythagorean cone: {(x,y,z) : min(x,y) = z, x ≤ y}.
    Bridge: connects TropicalGeometry (tropical varieties) to ConvexGeometry
    (polyhedral cones). -/
def tropicalPythCone : Set (ℝ × ℝ × ℝ) :=
  fun p => min p.1 p.2.1 = p.2.2 ∧ p.1 ≤ p.2.1

/-- Lipschitz constant for tropical Pythagorean distance.
    For ML certified robustness: the tropical distance between triples
    satisfies a Lipschitz bound with constant 1.
    Bridge: connects TropicalGeometry (ultrametric) to ML (certified_robustness). -/
def tropicalPythDist (p q : TropicalPythTriple) : ℝ :=
  max (|p.a - q.a|) (max (|p.b - q.b|) (|p.c - q.c|))
```

## Part IV: Cross-Domain Synthesis — Pythagorean Entropy and Post-Quantum Security

### Definitions Required

```lean4
/-- The Pythagorean counting function: number of primitive triples with
    hypotenuse ≤ N. Known asymptotic: π_P(N) ~ N/(2π).
    Bridge: connects AnalyticNumberTheory (counting functions) to
    InformationTheory (entropy of discrete distributions). -/
def pythCount (N : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Finset.card { p : PrimPythTriple // p.c ≤ N }

/-- The Pythagorean entropy: Shannon entropy of the uniform distribution
    on primitive triples with hypotenuse ≤ N.
```

**DOMAIN**: MachineLearning / CategoryTheory / InformationTheory

**CONCEPT**: Open the field of categorical deep learning by proving three foundational theorems establishing category theory as the natural language for representation learning, with explicit computational bounds connecting to certified robustness in ML and post-quantum lattice security via the categorical structure of homomorphic encryption functors.

### PART 1: Functorial Faithfulness Criterion and Yoneda Dimension

**Precise Formalization Target**: For a functor `F : C ⥤ D` between a finite data category `C` and a representation category `D` (enriched over `Vec K` for a field `K`), define "lossless representation" as: for every pair of distinct morphisms `f ≠ g` in `Hom_C(a, b)`, we have `F.map f ≠ F.map g` in `Hom_D(F.obj a, F.obj b)`. This is precisely faithfulness. The non-trivial content is:

**(Theorem 1) `yoneda_representation_dimension`**: For a faithful functor `F : C ⥤ Vec K` from a finite category `C`, the minimum embedding dimension `min_dim(F) = min {d : ℕ | ∃ (V : Type*) [FiniteDimensional K V], FiniteDimensional.finrank K V = d ∧ ∃ (G : C ⥤ Vec K) ≅ F, ∀ c, G.obj c = V}` satisfies `min_dim(F) ≤ |Ob(C)|` with equality if and only if the restricted Yoneda embedding `Y_C|_{Im(F)}` is full.

**(Theorem 2) `faithful_certified_robustness`**: Bridge: connects categorical representation to certified adversarial robustness. If `F : C ⥤ Vec K` is faithful and `K`-linear, then for any perturbation `δ : F.obj c →ₗ[K] F.obj c` with `‖δ‖_op < 1/(2·|Mor(C)|)`, the perturbed functor `F_δ` defined by `F_δ.obj c = F.obj c` and `F_δ.map f = F.map f + δ ∘ F.map f` remains faithful. This gives a certified robustness radius `r_cert = 1/(2·|Mor(C)|)` for categorical representations.

**Key Definitions to Formalize**:

```lean
/-- A representation functor with a certified faithfulness witness -/
structure CertifiedRepresentationFunctor (C : Type*) [Category C] (K : Type*) 
    [Field K] where
  F : C ⥤ Vec K
  faithful : Faithful F
  dim_bound : ℕ
  dim_cert : min_embedding_dim F ≤ dim_bound
  robustness_radius : ℝ
  certified_robust : ∀ (δ : ∀ c, F.obj c →ₗ[K] F.obj c),
    (∀ c, ‖δ c‖ ≤ robustness_radius) → Faithful (perturb F δ)

/-- The Yoneda representation rank of a functor -/
noncomputable def yonedaRank {C : Type*} [Category C] [Finite C] 
    {K : Type*} [Field K] (F : C ⥤ Vec K) : ℕ :=
  FiniteDimensional.finrank K (yonedaSpan F)

/-- Minimum embedding dimension for a faithful representation -/
noncomputable def minEmbeddingDim {C : Type*} [Category C] [Finite C]
    {K : Type*} [Field K] (F : C ⥤ Vec K) : ℕ :=
  sInf {d : ℕ | ∃ (V : Type*) [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V],
    FiniteDimensional.finrank K V = d ∧ Nonempty (F ≅ (constantFun V : C ⥤ Vec K))}
```

**Proof Strategy for `yoneda_representation_dimension`**:
1. **Lemma `yoneda_span_dimension`**: For a finite category `C` and functor `F : C ⥤ Vec K`, the span of all `F.map f` for `f ∈ Mor(C)` has dimension at most `|Ob(C)|²`. Prove by observing that the image of `F` is generated by at most `|Ob(C)|` objects, each contributing at most `|Ob(C)|` dimensions of morphisms.
2. **Lemma `faithful_yoneda_injective`**: If `F` is faithful, the restricted Yoneda map `Y_C|_{Im(F)} : C → [C^op, Set]` separates objects. Prove by contradiction using `by_contra`: if `Y_C(a) = Y_C(b)` for `a ≠ b`, then `Hom(-, a) ≅ Hom(-, b)`, so by Yoneda, `a ≅ b`, contradicting distinctness.
3. **Lemma `full_yoneda_maximal_dimension`**: If `Y_C|_{Im(F)}` is full, then `min_dim(F) = |Ob(C)|`. The fullness forces each object to contribute a full copy of the representation space.
4. **Main theorem**: Combine the upper bound from `yoneda_span_dimension` with the characterization from `full_yoneda_maximal_dimension`.

**Proof Strategy for `faithful_certified_robustness`**:
1. **Lemma `perturbation_faithfulness_criterion`**: A perturbed linear functor `F_δ` is faithful iff for all `f ≠ g` in `Hom_C(a,b)`, `‖(F.map f - F.map g) + δ ∘ (F.map f - F.map g)‖ ≥ ε` for some positive `ε`. Prove using the operator norm bound and the fact that `‖Id + δ‖ ≥ 1 - ‖δ‖ > 1/2` when `‖δ‖ < 1/2`.
2. **Lemma `faithfulness_gap`**: For faithful `F`, define `gap(F) = min_{f≠g} ‖F.map f - F.map g‖`. Then `gap(F) ≥ 1/|Mor(C)|` by pigeonhole on the unit ball. Use `omega` for the arithmetic.
3. **Main theorem**: If `‖δ‖ < 1/(2|Mor(C)|)`, then `‖(F.map f - F.map g) + δ ∘ (F.map f - F.map g)‖ ≥ gap(F) - ‖δ‖·gap(F) > gap(F)/2 > 0`, so `F_δ.map f ≠ F_δ.map g`. Use `linarith` for the final inequality.

**Precise Formalization Target**: For functors `F̂ F : C ⥤ Vec K` (learned and true data-generating functors), define the natural transformation distance and prove it bounds generalization error.

**Key Definitions**:

```lean
/-- Natural transformation distance between functors -/
noncomputable def natTransformDist {C : Type*} [Category C] {K : Type*} 
    [Field K] [NormedField K] (F̂ F : C ⥤ Vec K) : ℝ :=
  sInf {r : ℝ | ∃ (η : F̂ ⟹ F), ∀ c, ‖(η.app c : F̂.obj c →ₗ[K] F.obj c)‖ ≤ r}

/-- Categorical generalization error of a learned functor -/
noncomputable def categoricalGenError {C : Type*} [Category C] {K : Type*} 
    [Field K] (F̂ F : C ⥤ Vec K) : ℝ :=
  (∀ c, ‖F̂.obj c‖ + ‖F.obj c‖)⁻¹ · ∑ c : C, ‖F̂.obj c - F.obj c‖

/-- Certificate of unlearnability: no natural transformation exists -/
structure CategoricalUnlearnabilityCert {C : Type*} [Category C] {K : Type*} 
    [Field K] (F̂ F : C ⥤ Vec K) where
  no_nat_trans : ¬Nonempty (F̂ ⟹ F)
  obstruction : ∀ (η : ∀ c, F̂.obj c →ₗ[K] F.obj c),
```

### PART 3: Adjoint Autoencoder Theorem

**Precise Formalization Target**: An encoder-decoder pair `(E : C ⥤ Z, D : Z ⥤ C)` minimizing the information bottleneck objective `L = I(X; Z) - β·I(Z; X̂)` corresponds to an adjunction `E ⊣ D`.

**Key Definitions**:

```lean
/-- Information bottleneck objective for an encoder-decoder pair -/
structure InformationBottleneckObj (C Z : Type*) [Category C] [Category Z]
    [MeasurableSpace C] [MeasurableSpace Z] 
    (E : C ⥤ Z) (D : Z ⥤ C) where
  rate : ℝ  -- I(X; Z), the compression cost
  distortion : ℝ  -- I(Z; X̂), the reconstruction fidelity
  beta : ℝ  -- tradeoff parameter, 0 < beta < 1
  objective : rate - beta * distortion
  -- Certified bounds from adjunction structure
  reconstruction_error_bound : ℝ
  compression_bound : ℝ

/-- An adjoint autoencoder with certified information-theoretic bounds -/
structure AdjointAutoencoder (C Z : Type*) [Category C] [Category Z] 
    [NormedCategory C] [NormedCategory Z] where
  E : C ⥤ Z  -- encoder
  D : Z ⥤ C  -- decoder
  adj : E ⊣ D  -- adjunction witness
  unit_norm_bound : ∀ c, ‖(adj.unit.app c : C.Hom c (D.obj (E.obj c)))‖ ≤ √(1 - adj.beta)
  counit_norm_bound : ∀ z, ‖(adj.counit.app z : Z.Hom (E.obj (D.obj z)) z)‖ ≤ √(adj.beta)

/-- Normed category structure for representing data with metric -/
class NormedCategory (C : Type*) extends Category C where
  norm_hom : ∀ {a b : C}, (a ⟶ b) → ℝ
  norm_nonneg : ∀ {a b : C} (f : a ⟶ b), 0 ≤ norm_hom f
  norm_comp : ∀ {a b c : C} (f : a ⟶ b) (g : b ⟶ c), 
    norm_hom (g ≫ f) ≤ norm_hom g * norm_hom f
```
